payload.title: Outcome Echo: Mutation-Testing Result Feedback Loop
payload.description: After a mutation-testing run, the plugin writes a lightweight outcome record — which mutants actually escaped in CI vs. the agent's predictions — back to the logbook. The next run opens with that diff, so the agent recalibrates its 'kill confidence' scores instead of starting blind. Example: agent predicted 90% kill rate last sprint; actual was 61%; next invocation opens with that gap highlighted.

payload.title: Review Verdict Tracker: Did We Fix What Deep-Code-Review Found?
payload.description: Each deep-code-review finding gets a lightweight resolution slot in the logbook; on the next PR in the same repo, the plugin checks whether prior HIGH findings were addressed or silently repeated. If the same class of bug reappears, the review report opens with a 'repeat offender' callout instead of treating it as a first sighting. Example: null-dereference in PaymentService flagged twice — the second review shows the streak.

payload.title: Idea Survival Score: Track Which Ideation Seeds Get Built
payload.description: The ideation logbook appends a 'fate' field when a seed moves from idea to ticket, shipped feature, or archived. After a few sprints the plugin surfaces a survival rate per topic, letting the team see whether BOLD seeds ever ship or always die in planning. Example: logbooks-plugin topic shows 3/12 BOLD seeds shipped, 0/4 WILD seeds — a concrete signal to stop generating WILD ideas for this backlog.

payload.title: Cross-Plugin Trigger: Deep-Review Failure Spawns Ideation Session
payload.description: When deep-code-review surfaces 3+ HIGH findings on a single file across two consecutive PRs, it emits a structured event to a shared bus; the ideation plugin picks that event up and auto-seeds a 'refactor this hotspot' topic with the file path and repeated finding types pre-loaded. The developer gets an ideation session that already knows the pain point instead of starting from scratch. Example: PaymentService.java triggers an auto-seeded 'payment-refactor' topic.

payload.title: Private Outcome Hashing: Calibrate Without Exposing Code
payload.description: Instead of storing raw code snippets in the outcome log, the plugin hashes file paths and line ranges into opaque identifiers; the calibration logic works on hash-matched patterns, not readable source. Teams get cross-run learning without committing sensitive internals to the logbook. Example: a fintech team's compliance module paths are never readable in the logbook, but the agent still knows 'module pattern X historically escapes mutation at 40%'.

payload.title: Logbook Health Dashboard: One-Liner Status for Team Leads
payload.description: A new `logbook-status` command scans all active logbooks in the repo, outputs a single table: last write date, entry count, staleness flag, and which plugin owns it. A team lead running the command sees at a glance which plugins are actually being used and which logbooks have gone cold. Example: `mutation-testing` last wrote 2 days ago, 47 entries; `ideation` last wrote 14 days ago — likely stale.

payload.title: Segmented Memory: Per-Module Mutation Baselines
payload.description: Instead of one global kill-rate baseline, the mutation-testing plugin maintains a separate baseline per top-level module or package. When a new file is added to a module with a historically low kill rate, the report flags it as 'entering a high-risk zone' before CI even runs. Example: adding AuthService.java to the `auth/` module — which has a 55% historical kill rate — triggers an upfront warning.

payload.title: Inline Annotation Sync: Logbook Entries as Code Comments
payload.description: A post-review command lets the developer push selected deep-code-review findings as structured `// REVIEW[id]:` annotations directly into the source file, with the logbook entry ID embedded. The next review run strips resolved annotations automatically, keeping the logbook and the code in sync without a separate ticket system. Example: `// REVIEW[dcr-042]: null path in processPayment — unresolved` appears in the file until the finding is closed.

payload.title: Idea Hybridizer: Merge Two Seeds into a Third
payload.description: Given two seed IDs from the ideation logbook, a new `hybridize` sub-command generates a single combined idea that inherits constraints from both parents and writes it back as a child seed with `parent_ids` set. The provenance chain is queryable, so the team can see which original ideas spawned the thing they shipped. Example: hybrid of 'outcome hashing' + 'cross-plugin trigger' produces 'privacy-safe cross-plugin calibration bus'.

payload.title: Mutation Diff Alerts: Only Surface Regression, Not Full Report
payload.description: Instead of re-running and showing the full mutation report every time, the plugin computes a diff against the last run's results and surfaces only newly escaped mutants or newly killed ones. Developer attention is focused on what changed, not re-reading stable results. Example: 3 mutants escaped in `OrderService` since yesterday's run — a 4-line diff report instead of a 200-line full output.

payload.title: Logbook-Creator Auto-Schema Evolution: Add Column Without Migration Pain
payload.description: When a new field appears in 3+ consecutive logbook entries but isn't in the schema, the logbook-creator plugin detects the pattern and proposes a schema migration in-place, writing an ALTER entry to the logbook's own schema table. No external migration tool needed — the logbook bootstraps its own schema evolution. Example: reviewers keep adding a `severity_override` field ad hoc; the plugin surfaces 'promote this to a real column?' after the third occurrence.

payload.title: Sprint Retro Digest: Auto-Summary of All Plugin Logbooks
payload.description: A `retro-digest` command rolls up the last N days of entries across all plugin logbooks into a single structured summary: ideas generated vs. shipped, review findings opened vs. closed, mutation kill-rate trend. Paste it straight into the sprint retro doc. Example: 'Week of Apr 28: 12 seeds generated, 2 shipped; 8 HIGH review findings, 5 resolved; kill rate up 4% to 79%'.

payload.title: Coverage-Drift Gate
payload.description: Codecov blocks merges when line coverage drops below a threshold — transplant this to plugin suggestion quality: track a 'acceptance rate' per plugin over the last 30 runs and surface a warning badge when it falls more than 10 points from baseline. A dev sees 'mutation-testing plugin: 54% → 41% acceptance this week' right in the PR comment, same as a red coverage badge. Forces the team to notice when a plugin is giving worse advice, not just fewer answers.

payload.title: Deploy-Correlated Error Spikes
payload.description: Sentry pins error-rate spikes to the commit that caused them. Do the same for plugin invocations: each time a plugin run is logged, attach the current HEAD SHA so you can later correlate 'after commit abc123 the ideation plugin started producing 0 adopted ideas.' When someone does a post-mortem on a stale plugin, they get a timeline graph of adoption rate vs. git history, not just a flat average. This turns a vague 'it stopped working' into a concrete inflection point.

payload.title: Renovate-Style Merge-Habit Learning
payload.description: Renovate watches which dependency PRs you auto-merge vs. manually review and builds a per-repo policy. Apply this to plugin suggestions: silently track which output snippets get copy-pasted into actual files vs. discarded. After 20 runs, the plugin adjusts its output style — shorter if long outputs are rarely used, more specific if generic suggestions are always replaced. No config file needed; the habit is the config.

payload.title: Danger.js Inline Verdict Comments
payload.description: Danger.js posts structured rule violations directly into the PR diff as inline comments. Give each plugin a lightweight 'verdict formatter' that posts its key findings as inline comments on the exact lines that triggered them — a mutation-testing plugin annotates the survivor directly on the untested function, not in a separate report file. The signal lives where the developer is looking, not in a logbook they have to go find. One decorator on the plugin output, zero infra change.

payload.title: SonarQube Quality Gate as Plugin Exit Code
payload.description: SonarQube fails the CI step with a non-zero exit if the quality gate is breached — the pipeline stops, not just warns. Wire a configurable 'confidence floor' into plugin execution: if the plugin's own self-assessed confidence (already in many LLM outputs) is below threshold, it exits 1 and blocks the downstream step. A code-review plugin with 40% confidence on a security finding doesn't silently pass through to the PR merge step; the CI log shows exactly why it halted.

payload.title: GitHub Actions Reusable Workflow Registry
payload.description: GitHub lets teams publish reusable workflow templates to a central org registry so any repo can call them with a single `uses:` line. Build the same for logbooks plugins: a per-org plugin registry where a team publishes a tuned plugin version and other repos consume it with one config line. A platform team ships 'our company mutation-testing plugin v2' and all six product repos inherit it without copy-pasting YAML. The registry tracks which repo is on which version so the platform team can see adoption at a glance.

payload.title: Grafana Annotation Events on Plugin Runs
payload.description: Grafana lets you post deployment annotation markers onto any time-series chart so you can visually correlate 'we deployed v3' with a latency spike. Post a logbook annotation event every time a plugin runs, then render it as a vertical line on any chart of repo metrics (test coverage, PR cycle time, build duration). A team lead sees the correlation: 'mutation-testing plugin started running on Jan 15, PR review time dropped from 4h to 2.5h by Jan 30.' Causation is still your problem, but visibility is free.

payload.title: Dependabot Auto-PR for Stale Plugin Config
payload.description: Dependabot opens a PR the moment a dependency drifts from the allowed range, without anyone asking. Build a background job that watches plugin config files and opens a draft PR when a plugin hasn't been updated in 90 days or when a newer base model is available. The PR body shows a diff of what would change and the last three performance metrics, so the reviewer has enough context to merge or close in under two minutes. No more 'oh we're still running the June prompt' surprises six months later.

payload.title: Linear Triage Inbox for Plugin Findings
payload.description: Linear separates raw issue intake (Triage) from committed work (In Progress) so teams aren't overwhelmed. Give plugins a two-stage output: all findings first land in a 'plugin triage inbox' logbook that nobody has to act on, and only findings a human explicitly promotes get written to the active backlog. A security-scan plugin might surface 40 findings per run; the team picks 3 to promote this sprint. The inbox accumulates pattern data — which finding types get promoted most often — and the plugin learns to rank those higher.

payload.title: Semgrep Rule-Effectiveness Leaderboard
payload.description: Semgrep tracks which custom rules fire frequently vs. which are noise and surfaces that in a dashboard so teams prune dead rules. Build a per-plugin 'rule hit rate' leaderboard: each distinct finding type a plugin emits is a 'rule,' and the logbook tracks how often each was promoted to action vs. dismissed. A team sees 'suggestion type: extract-helper-function — 71% adoption; suggestion type: add-docstring — 9% adoption' and can toggle off the low-signal type without rewriting the plugin.

payload.title: DataDog SLO Budget Burn for Plugin Health
payload.description: DataDog's SLO burn-rate alerts fire not when an SLO is breached but when the budget is burning too fast to survive the window — an early warning, not a post-mortem. Define a plugin-health SLO as 'acceptance rate stays above 40% over 30 days' and compute a burn rate: if acceptance drops to 20% for three consecutive runs, the budget burns out in 8 days, not 30, so an alert fires now. The team gets a week to intervene instead of discovering the plugin was useless for a month.

payload.title: GitHub Actions Matrix Strategy for A/B Prompt Variants
payload.description: GitHub Actions matrix strategy runs the same job across N parameter combinations in parallel and collects a results table. Apply it to prompt variants: when a plugin config ships a new prompt, the runner forks two parallel executions — old prompt and new prompt — on the same input, logs both outputs, and after 10 paired runs shows a side-by-side acceptance-rate comparison in the PR that changed the prompt. The prompt author sees 'new variant: +12% adoption on mutation-testing tasks, -3% on refactoring tasks' before merge, not after.
